tagline: Count words, characters and reading time instantly as you type
pageDescription: Wondering how many words are in your text? Count words, characters, sentences and paragraphs in real time with this free online Word Counter. It works as a reading time calculator too, giving instant reading and speaking time estimates by word count as you type — perfect for writers, students, bloggers, and SEO professionals who need to hit exact length targets. A fast, no-signup alternative to Microsoft Word: secure and browser-based, your text never leaves your device.

instructions.title: How to use the Word Counter

steps.title: Type or paste your text
steps.description: Enter your text in the input box. Counts update live on every keystroke — no button to press.

steps.title: Read the live stats
steps.description: See words, characters (with and without spaces), sentences, paragraphs and lines update instantly as you write or edit.

steps.title: Check your reading time
steps.description: Reading time is estimated at 200 words per minute and speaking time at 130 words per minute, so you know how long your text takes to consume.

steps.title: Copy the statistics
steps.description: Click 'Copy stats' to copy a clean summary of all metrics to your clipboard for reports or submissions.

steps.title: Clear and start over
steps.description: Use the Clear button to empty the field and count a new piece of text from scratch.

proTips: Reading time uses 200 WPM (average adult silent reading); speaking time uses 130 WPM
Use 'Characters (no spaces)' for limits that exclude whitespace
Paragraphs are counted by blank lines, so separate blocks with an empty line
Emoji and accented characters count as a single character each
Paste directly from any editor — formatting is ignored, only text is counted
Copy stats to paste a clean metric summary into reports
troubleshooting: Word count looks off: extra spaces are ignored — only real words are counted
Paragraphs show as 1: separate paragraphs with a blank line, not a single newline
Sentence count unexpected: abbreviations with periods may be counted as sentence ends
Character count differs from another tool: this tool counts Unicode code points, so emoji count as 1
Nothing happens: counts update automatically — there is no button to click
